svg.title: On powers of degree at most two, Pan selects the quadratic coefficient; on powers of degree at most three, Flop selects the linear coefficient. The mixed selector is i Pana Flopb, evaluated on the specified two-direction momentum contour, with the corresponding powers of h−1. Its fixed finite coefficients bound it by a finite sum of the directional third coefficients just estimated. The local second selector is Pan on the opposed-momentum contour, with h−2. Analytic Taylor remainder bounds show that each selector differs from its indicated derivative coefficient by a term tending to zero as h →0, with mass restricted to a fixed [δ, 1]. For δ > 0, the massive matrices have a common positive lower bound, so their analytic inverse neighborhoods and the higher derivatives needed for these remainders are bounded throughout this interval. This also allows a mass μn depending on n. Absorb a final selector error at most 1 into μ−1 n, since μn ≤1.
